diagnostic_evidence.quote: Replacing $H^1$ by $H^\ell$ in the arguments from step 1 from \eqref{eq:h1_bound} onward, we get \eqref{e:hl_charac} for $\ell \in \bN$.
By part (ii) of \Cref{thm:hs_frac_charac}, this implies that $H^s$ is invariant under $\calK$ for all $s \in (0, \ell]$.

issues.failure_explanation: Condition (e:hl_charac) bounds d nu_{D^alpha phi}/dx in the H^{-|alpha|}-norms, but the written arguments only ever control the weaker H^{-ell}-norms. (a) Necessity: for |alpha|=ell the two norms coincide, but for |alpha|<ell the estimate with f in H^ell yields only ||z_{D^alpha phi}||_{H^{-ell}} <= C||phi||_{L^2}, and for alpha=0 the proof concludes only an H^{-1}-bound although (e:hl_charac) requires the stronger L^2=H^0-bound. Deriving the stated H^{-|alpha|}-bounds from H^ell-invariance needs boundedness of K on the intermediate spaces H^{|alpha|} (e.g. by interpolation between L^2 and H^ell), a nontrivial step that is missing. (b) Step 5 verifies only the uniform H^{-ell}-condition and then invokes part (ii), whose hypothesis is the stronger mixed-norm (e:hl_charac). All stated conclusions of (i)-(iii) remain true (necessity holds via interpolation; the weaker condition already suffices for the sufficiency direction and for (iii)), but they are not what the written arguments prove.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (e:hl_charac) with the uniform H^{-ell}-norm (replace H^{-|alpha|} by H^{-ell}); every proof in the paper is then correct as written and (i) remains a complete characterization, since the weaker condition is still equivalent to H^ell-invariance. If the sharper mixed-norm statement is to be kept, add the missing interpolation step (K bounded on L^2 by Lemma l:l2_invariance and on H^ell implies K bounded on H^{|alpha|} for all |alpha|<=ell, via the same interpolation theorem used in Step 3) plus the one-line bound ||d nu_phi/dx||_{L^2} = ||K_2^* phi||_{L^2} <= C||phi||_{L^2} for alpha=0.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if and only if' characterization of H^ell-invariance in part (i) is not established as stated, and the proof of part (iii) (restated as thm:diff_density_hs_invariance) invokes part (ii) with a condition that does not match (e:hl_charac). The invariance conclusions themselves (H^ell and H^s for s in (0,ell]) and all downstream error bounds remain valid: the weaker uniform-norm condition is exactly what the sufficiency arguments and the corollaries using (e:hl_charac) as a hypothesis require.
issues.title: Condition (e:hl_charac) is stated with H^{-|alpha|} norms, but the proofs only establish the weaker H^{-ell} bounds
issues.why_classification: The least severe resolution is a local correction of the norm index in (e:hl_charac) aligning the stated condition with what the proofs establish; after this edit the characterization, all invariance conclusions, and every error bound survive unchanged, with no new lemma, no reoptimization, and no loss of advertised content. (It is not a pure typo: the mismatch is only visible by checking the proof, and an alternative repair - keeping the statement and adding interpolation - exists.)

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\bH\subset C_b(\Omega)$ be a RKHS that is invariant under $\calK$.
Again, this gives the boundedness of $\calK: H^\ell \to H^\ell$ by \Cref{prop:RKHS_inv}

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:RKHS_inv (invariance implies boundedness) is proved only for reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces contained in C_b(Omega). For a bounded Lipschitz domain Omega subset R^n, H^ell(Omega) is an RKHS with continuous point evaluations (and a subset of C_b) only when ell > n/2; in particular H^1(Omega) is not contained in C_b(Omega) for any n >= 2. The necessity proof of Theorem thm:hs_frac_charac(i) invokes the proposition for H^1 (Step 1) and for general H^ell (Step 2), with the theorem stated for arbitrary n and ell, so for ell <= n/2 the boundedness of K on H^ell - needed, e.g., in (eq:h1_bound) and in the interpolation of part (ii) - is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: Then $\calK : H^1\to H^1$ is bounded by \Cref{prop:RKHS_inv}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the citation by the closed graph theorem: if f_n -> f in H^ell and K f_n -> g in H^ell, then f_n -> f and K f_n -> g in L^2, while K f_n -> K f in L^2 by Lemma l:l2_invariance, so g = K f; hence K is closed and therefore bounded on H^ell. The same bypass yields boundedness on H^s for s <= n/2 in thm:diff_density_hs_invariance.
issues.overall_effect: The boundedness assertions used inside the proof of thm:hs_frac_charac, and the boundedness claim K in L(H^s,H^s) of thm:diff_density_hs_invariance for s <= n/2 (whose proof routes through the same invariance-to-boundedness principle), are unjustified whenever the Sobolev order does not exceed n/2. The invariance statements and all error bounds downstream are unaffected once boundedness is established otherwise.
issues.title: Proposition prop:RKHS_inv is invoked for H^1/H^ell although these are not RKHS contained in C_b when ell <= n/2
issues.why_classification: The missing boundedness is restored by a short, standard closed-graph bypass using only Lemma l:l2_invariance; every conclusion (invariance, characterizations, error bounds) is preserved without new lemmas, without weakening any statement, and without touching the paper's main RKHS regime (sigma_{n,l} > n/2).

issues.failure_explanation: The second equality drops the factor 1/H on the first summand: with partial_1 G = (y-x)G and p = G/H, the quotient rule gives partial_1 p = (G(y-x)H - G H')/H^2 = p((y-x) - H'/H), not G((y-x) - H'/H^2). The subsequent bound is derived from the incorrect expression (and also bounds |H'|/H^2 by 1/(sqrt(2 pi) C_1) instead of 1/(sqrt(2 pi) C_1^2)). The correct derivative is still uniformly bounded on (0,1)^2, since 0 < C_1 <= H and |H'| <= 1/sqrt(2 pi), so condition (e:Hs_condition_density) for ell=1 still holds; the alpha=0 part (||p||_{L^2} <= 1/(sqrt(2 pi) C_1)) is immediate but is not accounted for in the stated constant C.

failure_location.quote: \partial_1 p(x,y) = \frac{\partial_1 G(x,y) H(x) - G(x,y) H'(x)}{H(x)^2} = G(x,y) \left( (y-x) - \frac{H'(x)}{H(x)^2}\right)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute partial_1 p = p((y-x) - H'(x)/H(x)) and bound |partial_1 p| <= (1/(sqrt(2 pi) C_1))(1 + 1/(sqrt(2 pi) C_1)); add the trivial estimate ||p||_{L^2((0,1)^2)} <= 1/(sqrt(2 pi) C_1) to cover the alpha=0 term of (e:Hs_condition_density).
issues.overall_effect: The verification of the sufficient condition (e:Hs_condition_density) in this example rests on a false computation; the proposition's conclusion (H^1-invariance for the truncated-normal transition kernel) remains true with the corrected bound, and nothing else in the paper depends on this example.
issues.title: Algebraically wrong derivative formula for partial_1 p in the truncated-normal example
issues.why_classification: The repair is routine algebra with the same bounding structure; the claim and its illustrative role for Theorem thm:hs_frac_charac(iii) are fully preserved, with no new argument and no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega\subset\R^n$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary

issues.failure_explanation: The chain is stated for the paper's general bounded Lipschitz domain Omega subset R^n, but several links fail for n >= 2: H^1(Omega) is not contained in C_b(Omega) (the embedding into C_b requires smoothness s > n/2, as the paper itself notes), and finite signed measures do not embed into H^{-1} = (H^1)^* (e.g. point evaluations are unbounded linear functionals on H^1 when n >= 2, so a Dirac measure is not in H^{-1}). Moreover, C_b(Omega)^* coincides with the finite regular Borel measures only for compact Omega, not for the open bounded domains considered here. The chain is valid only in dimension n = 1 (and the C_b^* = M identification only for compact Omega).

failure_location.quote: we have the following chain of inclusions with continuous embeddings $H^1\,\subset\,C_b\,\subset\,L^2\,\subset\,C_b^* = \calM\,\subset\,H^{-1}$, where $C_b^* = \calM$ is the space of all finite regular signed measures on $\Omega$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the chain to dimension n = 1, or replace H^1 by H^s with s > n/2, and state C_b^* = M only for compact Omega (or drop that identification).
issues.overall_effect: A false expository assertion. It is consistent with (and presumably motivates) the invalid application of prop:RKHS_inv to H^1 in the proof of thm:hs_frac_charac (ISSUE-002), but no formal statement or proof step relies on the chain itself.
issues.title: Embedding chain H^1 subset C_b subset L^2 subset C_b^* = M subset H^{-1} is false for the paper's general domains
issues.why_classification: A localized expository correction with no effect on any theorem, proof, algorithm, or error bound in the paper.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the paper's own construction B_{n,l}(x) = beta_{n,l}(||x||) with beta_{n,l} = I^l beta_{m}, m = floor(n/2)+l+1, direct computation gives B_{n,l}(0) = beta_{n,l}(0) = (2l)! m! / (2^l l! (m+2l)!). For example, B_{1,1}(0) = 1/12 (indeed beta_{1,1}(r) = (1/12)(1-r)_+^3(3r+1), consistent with the normalized kernel used in the numerics) and B_{3,1}(0) = 1/20, whereas the stated formula gives (1/2) binom(3,1) = 3/2 and (1/2) binom(4,1) = 2, respectively. The formula is incorrect for every l >= 1 (it coincides with the true value only for l = 0).

failure_location.quote: for the Wendland kernel $k_{n, l}$ with RBF $B_{n,l}$, we have $B_{n,l}(0) = \frac{1}{2^l} \binom{\lfloor n/2\rfloor + 2l + 1}{l}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by the correct value B_{n,l}(0) = (2l)! (floor(n/2)+l+1)! / (2^l l! (floor(n/2)+3l+1)!) (equivalently (2l-1)!! / prod_{j=1}^{2l}(m+j)), or state the value recursively via the operator I.
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicit constant in the eigenvalue discussion of rem:kernel_matrix_cond is false. The remark's inequality ||K_X^{-1} k_X(x)||_1^2 <= B(0) d/lambda_min(K_X) itself, and all error bounds in the paper (which use ||k||_infty or C_2 = sqrt(p_{n,l}(0)) abstractly), are unaffected.
issues.title: The explicit value B_{n,l}(0) of the Wendland radial basis function is wrong
issues.why_classification: A standalone false constant in a remark; correcting or removing it is a local edit, and no result, rate, or guarantee in the paper depends on the formula.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For numerical stability, we apply a Tikhonov regularization with parameter $\lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:regularized_mcemdmd}

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm lists the regularization parameter lambda among its required inputs but never uses it: the Koopman update applies the plain inverse K_X^{-1}, i.e. the unregularized estimator (eq:mcedmd). The surrounding text states that the experiments use the Tikhonov-regularized estimator (eq:regularized_mcemdmd) with (K_X + lambda I)^{-1}, and an adaptive choice of lambda is reported in the parameter table of Figure fig:linf_ou_const_vs_adapt_left_right. As specified, the procedure's operation does not match its input contract nor the method it is said to summarize.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use (K_X + lambda I)^{-1} in place of K_X^{-1} in the update (or remove lambda from the list of required inputs).
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm block does not implement the regularized estimator analyzed in cor:mc_error1_tikh and cor:reg_total_err_bound and used in the experiments; a reader implementing the block as written would not reproduce the described method. The theoretical error bounds are unaffected (both lambda = 0 and lambda > 0 are covered).
issues.title: Algorithm 1 requires a regularization parameter lambda as input but implements the unregularized estimator
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the update (or of the input list) restores the contract; no mathematical content is lost since both estimator variants and their guarantees are already established in the paper.
